hotspots.topic: GFCI vs. Assured Equipment Grounding Conductor Program
hotspots.whyItMatters: This is the signature OSHA-electrical topic for construction: temporary cord-and-plug equipment must be protected by ONE of two compliant methods, not both.
hotspots.trap: Believing GFCI protection and the assured equipment grounding conductor program are both required together — the standard treats them as alternative, either/or compliance paths.

hotspots.whyItMatters: De-energizing before work on exposed parts is the core 'qualified person' safety doctrine tested throughout this book.
hotspots.trap: Treating a tag alone as sufficient control without a physical lock, or skipping the try-before-you-touch verification step after lockout is applied.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Broad language protecting employees from exposed energized parts underlies many scenario-style questions.
hotspots.trap: Assuming a cord or tool that still 'works' is compliant even though its insulation is visibly damaged — the rule is about condition, not function.

hotspots.whyItMatters: The 300/300A/301 forms and their posting/retention duties are a distinct recordkeeping question set, separate from safety-practice questions.
hotspots.trap: Confusing the annual summary posting window with the multi-year retention period, or forgetting which employer sizes are exempt from routine recordkeeping.

hotspots.whyItMatters: The short reporting clocks (fatality vs. hospitalization/amputation/eye loss) are a favorite 'which number is it' question.
hotspots.trap: Assuming a single reporting deadline covers everything — a fatality and an in-patient hospitalization/amputation/eye-loss report are on two different clocks keyed to severity, so look up which one applies before you assume the timing.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Employer duties to assess hazards and provide PPE are a recurring general-safety subject that crosses into every trade.
hotspots.trap: Assuming PPE is only required where the hazard is 'obvious' instead of after a documented hazard assessment.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Ladder setup and use rules show up under the tools/testing side of this exam subject.
hotspots.trap: Setting a portable ladder by feel instead of the required setup angle, and forgetting the separate rule that the side rails must extend above the landing point — verify both against the standard.

hotspots.whyItMatters: A distinct construction-electrical hazard topic — ventilation and facility protection around charging areas, not just PPE.
hotspots.trap: Treating battery-charging hazards as generic chemical storage instead of the specific ventilation and facility-protection duties this section actually imposes.
